items.prompt: The top of a fraction tells us how many parts are counted, and the bottom number tells us what kind of parts they are. So, here’s a fraction.  5/6
items.demo: The bottom number is six, so these are *sixths*.

items.prompt: The top number is five, so five sixths are counted.  5/6
items.demo: So *five sixths* make up this fraction.
These are still sixths, but now four are counted. So *four sixths* make up this fraction.
Now these are sevenths, and four are counted. So *four sevenths* make up 4/7. Each time, the bottom number names the parts, and then the top number tells us how many of those parts are counted.

items.demo: *Six* sixths make up one whole unit.
